lesson.title: Procedure 504 – SOLO UNIT PROCEDURE
lesson.topic: Radio Dispatcher – Solo Unit Handling & Assignments
objectives: Identify which event types are appropriate for one-officer (solo) handling under Procedure 504.
Correctly interpret expansion codes and meanings for solo-appropriate event types, including TRANSIT and LMT AC HWY variations.
Apply solo unit designation rules (extra 'S') and correctly map two-officer designations to solo designations.
Apply backup dispatching requirements and restrictions for two-officer type incidents and potentially violent situations.
Use correct lineup-change process when converting between solo and two-officer designations (10-61, LOU).

questions.stem: Which statement correctly reflects Procedure 504 guidance on solo units?

choices.text: Any available Precinct or Department unit may provide the backup (anti-crime, special unit, supervisors, etc.).
Solo unit designations will use an extra 'S' in the resource identification.
Two-officer event types within the solo sector should be assigned to the solo unit only when a backup unit is sent; do not enter an assignment until it is certain a backup unit is also responding.
A solo unit may be used as a backup unit for other sectors when no other closer units are available and for nearby solo events when no other units are available.
